R299.note: Removing the file read behind an allowlisted-key lookup closes the vector, but the keys (standard/premium/enterprise) and rate values are invented constants rather than the configured rates, so any real approved key now throws; the swap is stated but not flagged as placeholder data needing a follow-up.

R300.note: RFC 4515 escaping of *, (, ), backslash and NUL on the cn value neutralises filter injection with no other observable change.

R301.note: Dropping the template.HTML wrapper and typing Body as string restores html/template context-aware escaping; nothing else changes.

R302.note: CGI::escapeHTML on the free-text subject at the sink is the right call; priority and ticket_id are correctly left alone as allowlisted/server-generated.

R303.note: Resolving base and candidate then checking is_relative_to blocks absolute-path, traversal and symlink escapes; the added 403 for out-of-base requests is the fix's own response and blocks no legitimate file.

R304.note: Named HQL parameter with the wildcards applied to the bound value preserves the contains-search semantics exactly.

R305.note: Gate::authorize enforces the policy that the ignored Gate::allows result never did; the 403 on failure is the intended behaviour.

R306.note: CSRFProtect plus FlaskForm/validate_on_submit is the right mechanism, but the token is only emitted if account_settings.html renders form.csrf_token or hidden_tag(), and the write-up claims this is automatic instead of calling out the template (and any other POST form in the app) as a required change - until updated, legitimate submissions get 400.

R307.note: Parameterised @Owner via AddWithValue closes the injection; only edge is a null owner now surfacing as a missing-parameter error rather than an empty result.

R308.note: Extension allowlist matches the endpoint's stated document-only purpose and is declared as a product decision; the exact list ('etc.') still needs confirming against what the product actually accepts.

R309.note: Allowlist map breaking taint before call_user_func_array is the right shape, but the verbs and handler names (handleStatusCommand etc.) are invented and no such functions exist in the case, so real commands are rejected as unknown until the map is populated, and the write-up does not say so.

R310.note: jwt.verify closes the signature bypass, but the hardcoded 'your-secret-key' fallback means an unconfigured deployment verifies against a guessable secret (attacker-forgeable tokens); stated in the write-up but not flagged as a placeholder that must fail closed.

R311.note: realpath on base and target plus a component-aware path.relative check contains the read; null-byte/non-string rejection and 403/404 mapping block nothing legitimate.

R312.note: resolve + relative containment closes traversal; startsWith('..') would also reject a legitimate file literally named ..something, an exotic edge not worth a deduction.

R313.note: sqlite3 ? placeholder with a bound tuple is the correct fix; integer-affinity comparison still matches numeric ids.

R314.note: Lazy %s formatting with repr() escapes newlines and other control characters; the resulting quoted username in every log line is a format change but is stated plainly and breaks nothing.

R315.note: secure: true closes CWE-614; the added sameSite: 'lax' is stated hardening that still allows the top-level SSO redirect flow.
